articles.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 3: Latest news, updates for Caleb Williams, Jaxson Dart, more with fantasy football analysis
articles.summary: We're going over the Week 3 NFL injury report to help with your fantasy football lineup decisions.
articles.body:
The NFL injury report is starting to get crowded as we head into Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. Among those injured in Week 2 was Bears QB Caleb Williams, who suffered what appeared to be a pretty bad lower-body injury at the time . Turns out, Williams sustained a hamstring injury that has him week-to-week going into a matchup vs. the Eagles on Monday Night Football.

On top of that, the Commanders could be without QB Jayden Daniels long-term after he suffered another elbow injury — something he dealt with last season — in the team's loss to the Cowboys in Week 2. And then on MNF, the Giants lost starter Jaxson Dart to a knee injury that could hold him out. It's tough out there in the QB fantasy streets.

We'll be monitoring their statuses moving forward, as well as a handful of notable players for fantasy football in Week 3.

Jaxson Dart, NYG (knee) — Could miss rest of season

Kyler Murray , MIN (concussion) — Will Play

Michael Penix Jr., ATL (knee) — Will Start Week 3

Dart : The Giants got the worst news possible later on Monday as the injury for Dart is more serious than initially thought. He's going to miss an extended period of time, which could be the entire 2026 season, per ESPN . Jameis Winston struggled in relief on Monday, completing just 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and one INT. As a result, the Giants only mustered 183 total yards (some of those were before Dart got hurt). This is a major downgrade for Giants' skill position players, namely Malik Nabers , Cam Skattebo and Isaiah Likely . Though, New York does have a solid matchup in Week 3 vs. the Titans at home. It's tough to see this offense staying afloat with Winston at the helm all season.

Bagent : Things just got a bit worse for the Bears and Ben Johnson. Bagent has been placed into the NFL's concussion protocol and now his status for Week 3 vs. the Eagles on MNF is up in the air. He'll have the extra day to clear, but it's usually pretty tough to do so in this little amount of time. If Bagent can't start, Chicago will turn to Case Keenum right now. It's unclear who would be promoted to serve as his backup or if the Bears would opt to bring someone else in to possibly start. This is just another QB injury we'll need to monitor closely this week.

Penix : The Falcons cleared Penix for Week 3's matchup vs. the Packers on Thursday Night Football. He will be welcome addition to the offense, which has struggled mightily in two games with Cooper Rush/Jack Strand under center. With Penix in the lineup, it should be a huge boost for pass-catchers Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr., as well as star RB Bijan Robinson .

Williams : As was stated above, Williams is week-to-week with the hamstring issue, which is a great sign that he avoided major injury. The Bears will likely proceed with Tyson Bagent at QB in Week 3 vs. the Eagles, assuming Williams can't play. Head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Williams will "likely miss some time." Bagent is a serviceable backup who has shown flashes of decent play in the past. But he's a very clear downgrade from Williams. Chicago pass-catchers Rome Odunze , Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland had already been underperforming through two weeks. They'll carry a significant amount of risk in Week 3 should Williams sit. We could see Johnson lean more heavily on RBs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai in the short-term.

Daniels : The Commanders' signal-caller is dealing with a dislocated left elbow but doesn't have a fracture, which is a positive. Still, it's the same injury he suffered last season in Week 9. We don't have a timeline on a return for Daniels, but backup Marcus Mariota should start in Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. For this week, with such a difficult matchup, it may be wise to fade Washington entirely. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs would be risky flex options, even in PPR formats. In easier matchups, Mariota has shown the ability to buoy the offense, and he did find Diggs for a TD in Week 2 after Daniels left.

Murray : Kyler has cleared concussion protocol and will start for the Vikings in Week 3 vs. the Bucs . It's difficult to gather anything from Week 2's 9-3 win over the Bears given the weather. We also only saw Murray for barely a series before he exited in Week 1 vs. the Packers. We'll have to see how he fares before making any type of assessment. For now, Murray is more of a QB2 until we know more. Luckily, there have been plenty of QBs who have emerged as strong fantasy options you can likely scoop up off the waiver wire .

Broncos backfield : Harvey was inactive for the Broncos' win over the Jaguars in Week 2. Dobbins exited the game early, which paved the way for rookie Jonah Coleman to have a larger role. He's going to be a trendy waiver wire claim going into Week 3. Justin Boone has more on Coleman and how to approach him off the wire here .

Barkley : We're awaiting more information on Barkley's stinger, which caused him to miss a big chunk of the comeback win over the Titans on Sunday. As a result, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches for 38 yards and a score. Should Barkley miss any time, Bigsby would become the lead back with Will Shipley also in the mix. Bigsby is another name Boone mentions as a top waiver consideration for Week 3.

Price : You're going to sense a trend here. Price left in the fourth quarter of the Seahawks' easy win over the Cardinals in Week 2. This injury doesn't appear to be serious, so there's a chance Price is good to go for Week 3 vs. the Commanders. It's worth noting Emanuel Wilson was heavily involved in Week 2, rushing 21 times for 92 yards. George Holani also got five touches. Price did lose a fumble in the game but should remain the focal point of the rushing attack when healthy. If you have Price, it's worth adding Wilson just in case. If Price is sidelined, Wilson would get a solid boost into RB2/3 territory.

Nacua : The Rams sat Nacua on MNF in Week 2 vs. the Giants. It led to a massive performance from Davante Adams , who hauled in eight of 10 targets for 195 yards and two TDs. He finished as the WR2 in fantasy, trailing only Jaxon Smith-Njigba and his hat trick from Sunday. HC Sean McVay is hopeful Nacua can suit up in Week 3 vs. the Broncos. If Nacua remains out, Adams is a borderline WR1, though he draws a tough matchup vs. Pat Surtain II. Terrance Ferguson would also be more involved after his solid 6-54-1 line vs. New York.

Nabers : The wide receiver exited MNF vs. the Rams after his shoulder got dislocated . He popped it back in and was able to return to the game, stating that he's "OK" post-game. Nabers is schedule to undergo X-rays, so we'll wait and see what the results show. For now, monintor Nabers' status during practice but know that with Dart sidelined, his fantasy value takes a pretty big hit. Tennessee presents a good matchup in Week 3, but Nabers should be downgraded to a risky WR2/3 in PPR formats.

Collins : The Texans were without Collins for their tough loss to the Bengals in Week 2. The offense struggled, clearly missing its top wideout and target for C.J. Stroud . TE Dalton Schultz was the biggest beneficiary, finishing as the TE2 overall in fantasy after Sunday, catching 12 of 14 targets for 140 yards. Houston has a big game vs. the Colts in Week 3 and the expectation is for Collins to remain out . Indy has allowed 74 points through two games this season, so there's a good chance the Texans can get something going, which could bode well for Xavier Hutchinson , Kayshon Boutte and Jaylin Noel .

Moore : The Bills wideout is considered day-to-day with an AC joint sprain. He's had extra time to get right after suffering the injury on TNF vs. the Lions in Week 2. If Moore is active, he's a solid WR2/3 in a good matchup vs. the Chargers. If Moore is out, Keon Coleman , Khalil Shakir and Josh Palmer should get the majority of the snaps at WR. Dalton Kincaid has been Josh Allen 's favorite target so far this season and that should continue with or without Moore in Week 3.

Pierce : The Colts wide receiver was forced to exit TNF vs. the Chiefs after aggravating the same heel/ankle injury that kept him sidelined during training camp . There's no clear timeline for Pierce's return. If Pierce misses time, it's a bump up for Josh Downs and Tyler Warren . Laquan Treadwell shockingly saw 74% of the snaps in the loss to the Chiefs, which was more than veteran Keenan Allen , who only caught one of his five targets for five yards.

Goedert : The Eagles' pass-catcher is expected to miss a few weeks after spraining his MCL in Week 2 vs. the Titans, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. After finishing as a TE1 last season, Goedert got off to a hot start with 4-77-2 in Week 1 to finish as the TE2 overall. He had just one catch for four yards before leaving on Sunday. Philly is now down its top-two TEs in Goedert and rookie Eli Stowers , who is on injured reserve with a hamstring issue. Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins split the snaps at TE vs. Tennessee, and Mundt was targetted three times. He isn't really a viable streaming option at TE if you have Goedert, so look to Boone's waiver wire guide for Week 3 for advice . The Eagles offense is getting pretty banged up, which isn't great. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks should continue to lead the passing game, though don't sleep on Darius Cooper .

Bowers : Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters after the team's win in Week 2 that Bowers is "very close" to returning. That could mean we see him suit up in Week 3 vs. the Saints, though with Las Vegas 2-0 to start the season, the team could be cautious with the top pass-catcher. With Bowers out again, it was Michael Mayer who got the majority of the TE snaps at 84%. Cody White isn't technically a tight end but he caught two TDs that likely would have been layups for Bowers had he been healthy. Mayer will continue to be a decent streaming option at TE in Week 3 if Bowers sits again. There should be plenty of points in the Saints-Raiders matchup.

Ricky Pearsall , WR, SF (knee) — Out for season

Jayden Higgins , WR, HOU (knee) — Out for season

Ja'Kobi Lane, WR,BAL (wrist) — Injured reserve

Jordan Mason , RB, MIN (thumb) — Injured reserve

De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, SF (ankle) — Injured reserve

Omar Cooper Jr., WR, NYJ (ankle) — Injured reserve

A.J. Brown , WR, NE (ankle) — Injured reserve

Jordyn Tyson, WR, NO (hamstring) — Injured reserve

Dylan Sampson , RB, CLE (knee) — Injured reserve

David Njoku , LAC (knee) — Injured reserve

Charlie Kolar , LAC (forearm) — Injured reserve

Zach Charbonnet , RB, SEA (knee) — PUP list

articles.title: Devin Booker's Possible Regression Isn’t Concern for Phoenix Suns
articles.summary: Skeptics question Devin Booker’s superstar trajectory as Phoenix faces looming roster uncertainties, testing whether the franchise cornerstone can overcome a...
articles.body:
The 2026-27 season is right around the corner for the Phoenix Suns .

Phoenix is just one month away from tipping the regular season off with a road game against the Portland Trail Blazers .

While internal expectations and hopes from the fans are quite lofty, the outside world doesn't seem to be showing the team quite the same amount of love.

Part of this ensemble is Kevin O'Connor of Yahoo Sports, who ranks the Suns as the 20th best team in the NBA heading into training camp.

The 15-20 range seems to be a customary placing for Phoenix at the moment, but O'Connor's concern is perhaps the most jarring part of the evaluation of the Suns.

"Can Booker get back to superstar form?"

There's little doubt that franchise star Devin Booker has experienced a slight downtick in scoring volume and efficiency as of late.

Even if Booker isn't a top-five level scorer any longer - or hasn't reached the heights that the 2023 postseason run demonstrated he can reach - he is still one of the best players in the league.

The 6'5" shooting guard is still evolving as a playmaker, is still one of the craftiest scorers in the entire league, and presents gravity that creates advantages for rising stars such as Collin Gillespie .

Is Booker a perfect player? Absolutely not. However, it feels trivial to question his ability to lead a team in 2026, especially after the five-time All-Star led Phoenix to a playoff appearance in a season that multiple co-stars missed extensive time due to injury. The question shouldn't be framed around Booker's decline, it should be as to whether the Kentucky product has an ability to become a ceiling raiser yet again.

Phoenix has several other concerns that are much more pressing than Booker. Among these concerns are the uncertain center rotation with the absence of Mark Williams . There is also the question if the Suns will be able to capture the exceptional three-point shooting magic they did in 2025-26. Beyond this, the fit of incoming forward Miles Bridges and guard Luke Kennard is one that will test head coach Jordan Ott.

Even if one wants to state that Booker is regressing, this is far from the most substantial concern at the moment for the Suns' organization. This will become apparent very early in the season for those that are skeptical about this conversation.

articles.title: Charlotte Hornets jersey history No. 3 Hersey Hawkins 1993-1995
articles.summary: Hersey Hawkins played three seasons with the Charlotte Hornets in two separate stints with the franchise.
articles.body:
Hersey Hawkins played for the Charlotte Hornets in two different stints, wearing three different jersey numbers (No. 3, No. 32 and No. 33) during his tenure. After averaging 19 points per game in his first five seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers , the Hornets acquired Hawkins ahead of the 1993-94 campaign.

Hawkins played all 82 games for Charlotte in two consecutive seasons, averaging 14.3 points, 4.2 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.6 steals while shooting 47.1% from the field and 39.2% from 3-point range. The Hornets later included Hawkins in a trade package to the Seattle SuperSonics for Kendall Gill. After four seasons with Seattle and one with the Chicago Bulls , Hawkins signed a one-year deal with the Hornets and finished his career in Charlotte. In 59 games for the Hornets the second time around, Hawkins averaged 3.1 points, 1.4 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.6 steals.

The former No. 6 overall pick finished his 13-year NBA career with one All-Star appearance, a sportsmanship award and averages of 14.7 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.7 steals.

articles.title: Mike Macdonald's comments about Sean Payton weren't intended for public consumption
articles.summary: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald launched his career as a head coach with a win over Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald launched his career as a head coach with a win over Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos . The game from September 2024 moved back to the front burner on Tuesday, thanks to footage from Macdonald's recent interview with Graham Bensinger.

The excerpt , which wasn't released when the first clips and quotes began to be circulated, relates to a squabble that emerged regarding the use by the Seahawks of fan-generated video from Broncos training-camp practices. It got ugly , as Macdonald told the story to Bensinger.

It could get ugly between the Seahawks and Bensinger's camp. As we understand it, the conversation was not intended by Macdonald for public consumption. The Seahawks, we're told, didn't even know that portion of the "more off than on" the record discussion had been recorded until Tuesday morning.

The situation is another reminder that everything is potentially on the record, absent a clear agreement between the parties that it's not. And while Bensinger's people didn't breach any journalistic rules by using it, the fact that it was posted could make future subjects more leery about agreeing to be interviewed.

On or off the record, others are befuddled by Macdonald's decision to air gripes from two years ago. And there's a question as to whether the various things Macdonald said to Bensinger (regarding Payton and others) are the product of arrogance or naiveté.

"What's the point?" said one source connected to neither the Seahawks nor the Broncos. "It was reckless."

The Broncos declined comment on the situation. Undoubtedly, Payton will be asked about it when he conducts his usual Wednesday press conference.

Either way, the kerfuffle adds a little extra sizzle to a spicy Week 6 Thursday night game between the two teams.

articles.title: Kansas freshman Taylor Stanley named AVCA Player of the Week
articles.summary: LAWRENCE (KSNT) – Taylor Stanley has continued to impress since arriving in Lawrence for her freshman season. The freshman pin hitter has been named the Amer...
articles.body:
LAWRENCE ( KSNT ) - Taylor Stanley has continued to impress since arriving in Lawrence for her freshman season.

The freshman pin hitter has been named the American Volleyball Coaches Association (AVCA) Player of the Week. She was also named the Big 12 Rookie and Offensive Player of the Week.

Stanley is the first Jayhawk to receive the honor since Kelsie Payne in 2016. She helped the No. 19 Jayhawks to a 3-0 week with sweeps against Wichita State, Ole Miss and Grand Canyon.

Stanley posted 48 kills and 5.33 kills per set while having a .456 attack percentage. She leads the Big 12 and is fourth nationally in points per set at 5.70, and is second in the conference and fifth in the country with 4.74 kills per set.

Stanley and the Jayhawks are back in action at 6 p.m. on Friday, Sept. 25, to open up Big 12 play against Houston.

articles.title: Things will only go from bad to worse for Chargers against red-hot Josh Allen, Bills
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are embarrassing themselves in front of the entire football community. There really isn’t a nicer way to put it after two weeks. The...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are embarrassing themselves in front of the entire football community.

There really isn't a nicer way to put it after two weeks. The Chargers entered the season with legitimate Super Bowl expectations after an aggressive offseason, yet they are 0-2 after consecutive 26-14 losses to the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders . Neither game looked like an unfortunate loss, either. Los Angeles has looked unprepared, undisciplined, and completely lost for extended stretches.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Chargers now travel to Buffalo to face Josh Allen and a Bills team that looks absolutely terrifying. Buffalo has scored 77 points through two games, including 41 against Detroit on Thursday night, and Allen already looks like he's building another MVP-caliber season.

That's the last opponent Los Angeles needs right now.

Mike McDaniel 's offense has been a mess through two games. The offensive line has struggled to consistently protect Justin Herbert , receivers aren't creating enough separation, and Herbert has responded by forcing throws he normally wouldn't make. He deserves some of the blame, too. Herbert hasn't consistently recognized pressure quickly enough and threw two interceptions against Las Vegas while completing only 15 of 27 passes.

But the Chargers aren't exactly helping their franchise quarterback. The penalties, turnovers, protection breakdowns and general confusion make it look like an offense still trying to figure out what it wants to be. Now David Njoku and Charlie Kolar are both headed to injured reserve , removing two tight ends from an offense that desperately needs reliable options.

That's before even getting to the defense.

Chargers' defense might be walking into a nightmare against Josh Allen

Chris O'Leary inherited a defense that Jesse Minter helped turn into one of the NFL's better units over the previous two seasons. Through two games, however, Los Angeles hasn't looked nearly as aggressive or disruptive.

The Chargers have frequently kept their secondary deep and asked their defensive front to create pressure without consistently bringing additional rushers. That can work when Khalil Mack , Tuli Tuipulotu , and Akheem Mesidor are taking over games. Outside of flashes, that hasn't happened enough yet, and Los Angeles hasn't consistently forced opposing quarterbacks into uncomfortable situations.

Trying that against Allen sounds like a disaster waiting to happen.

Allen just shredded Detroit for 248 passing yards and three touchdowns while adding 69 rushing yards and two more scores. Buffalo scored touchdowns on five of its first six possessions and built a 27-10 halftime advantage against a Lions team that entered the season with championship aspirations.

The Chargers are supposed to slow that down? This defense could get carved up like a pumpkin pie on Thanksgiving if they don't change something up quickly.

Los Angeles is also dealing with injuries defensively, including Derwin James playing through a finger issue . Asking an already struggling defense to contain Allen, James Cook , and Buffalo's collection of weapons without generating immediate pressure could turn Sunday's game ugly very quickly. Look for former Chargers receiver Josh Palmer to make a play or two.

Herbert might have to become Los Angeles' version of Allen just to keep the Chargers competitive. Buffalo's defense has allowed 31 points in each of its first two games, so opportunities should exist for McDaniel and Herbert to finally get the offense moving. The problem is that Buffalo's pass rush has already produced seven sacks, creating another brutal matchup for a Chargers offense struggling with protection.

This isn't necessarily a must-win game in September, but 0-3 would create a hole nobody expected Los Angeles to be digging out of this early.

The Chargers spent the offseason convincing everyone they were ready to contend with the AFC's best.

They're about to find out exactly how far away they really are.

articles.title: DBacks vs Rockies updates. Desperation time in Denver, chasing wild card
articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks began their final regular-season road trip of 2026 on Tuesday, Sept. 22, in Denver. Follow our live updates.
articles.body:
DENVER — The Diamondbacks came into their game on Tuesday, Sept. 22, against the Rockies at Coors Field in need of six wins, in their minds, over their final six games of the regular season to have a shot at a National League wild-card spot.

They entered the night four games behind the Philadelphia Phillies and five behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres .

"Focus on what we do well, focus on doing your job and not worrying about anything else," Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said prior to the first of three games against Colorado . "Little things matter. Do little things and let them add up to a big moment.

"We know what we've got to do. We've got to go out and win every baseball game. I don't like thinking like that. I just want us to win today. I want us to play our finest game today and at the end of the day, we'll see where we're at."

Ketel Marte , who has a history of not playing an entire series when the Diamondbacks visit Colorado due to health reasons, was in the lineup as the designated hitter. Lovullo said he planned to have Marte play defense the last two games of the series.

"I don't want to ask anybody to go out there and empty their tank," Lovullo said. "We know what we've got to get to, and I'm going to ask guys to go and give me just a little bit extra."

See Arizona Diamondbacks' 3-game series vs New York Yankees in photos

Burnes to remain in rotation, Moreno's workload

The Diamondbacks, if they stick with how they've set up their pitching rotation, will turn to right-hander Corbin Burnes on Saturday, Sept. 26, at San Diego in what could still be a game to stay alive in the wild-card race.

"We'll probably just trust what he's given us and his own personal evaluation. He feels strong, he feels healthy," Lovullo said of Burnes, who spent 15 months trying to get back from elbow surgery and a subsequent injury.

Catcher Gabriel Moreno continues to play without much rest at all. Moreno is so vital to the Diamondbacks with his consistent hitting and defense that Lovullo continues to go to him.

"He's in that category where you can't win games without him," Lovullo said. "We've got to manage his workload. I caught him three days in a row before the off day (Monday). I haven't done that all year long. He's going to probably catch five of the last six games, depending on what the needs are.

"In the game that he doesn't catch, I'm probably going to DH him. But he's been so impactful for us."

Moreno said the key for him to have reached career highs in games played, at-bats, runs scored, hits, home runs and runs batted in is staying healthy this season. Tuesday was Moreno's 126th game of the season, out of 157.

"Just going to do my best in everything I can," Moreno said. "Running, hitting, catching, helping the team win."

Diamondbacks at Rockies, 5:40 p.m., Cox, Ch. 34

Diamondbacks RHP Michael Soroka (8-5, 3.45) vs. Rockies LHP Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.38)

At Coors Field : Soroka gave up one run in five innings against the Marlins in his most recent start, giving up just two hits, one of which was a solo homer by RF Griffin Conine . … It was his second outing off the injured list. In his first one, he allowed three homers in four innings in a loss at Kansas City . … He has faced the Rockies three times this season, giving up just three runs in 16 innings for a 1.69 ERA. … Freeland, 33, has pitched 10 seasons in the majors, all with the Rockies, but this could be his final start in Colorado, with his contract set to expire at the end of the year. … Freeland gave up three runs in four-plus innings against the Padres in his most recent start. … He has faced the Diamondbacks 23 times in his career and has posted a 6.28 ERA. The Diamondbacks hit him hard earlier this season, scoring seven times off him in 3 2/3 innings.

Wednesday, Sept. 23: At Colorado, 5:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00) vs. Rockies RHP Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09).

Thursday, Sept. 24: At Colorado, 12:10 p.m., Diamondbacks LHP Eduardo Rodriguez (15-7, 2.89) vs. Rockies RHP Tanner Gordon (1-5, 6.01).

Friday, Sept. 25: At San Diego, 6:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.72) vs. Padres RHP Casey Mize (6-9, 3.96).
